t061.sum: Mercy is justice tempered by wisdom that fully knows the weaknesses and handicaps of creatures. God is merciful by nature and needs no one to persuade him; the Eternal Son is mercy itself, and the Infinite Spirit ministers that mercy throughout the universe. Mercy does not violate justice but applies it with understanding, and man learns true mercy by passing through justice, fairness, patience, and kindness.
t061.s1.i2: Even divine justice, which lets wrongdoing reap its results, is always tempered by mercy, in proportions determined by infinite wisdom.
t061.s1.i3: Mercy is not a contravention of justice but an understanding interpretation of supreme justice as fittingly applied to evolving finite creatures.
t061.s1.i4: When eternal justice and divine mercy work together, what man calls fairness emerges in human experience.
t061.s1.i5: God is not torn between justice and mercy; in his omniscience he fully satisfies both demands at once.
t061.s2.h: Mercy Flowing from the Father's Nature
t061.s2.i2: Mercy is the natural offspring of goodness and love; a loving father cannot withhold mercy from his children.
t061.s2.i3: It is an error to think that the Eternal Son pleads with the Father for mercy; all the Son's mercy is a direct revelation of the Father's love.
t061.s2.i4: God harbors no feelings of wrath or vengeance; such attitudes are inconsistent with the Father's merciful character.
t061.s2.i5: Even a rebel who turns to righteousness is received in mercy, and God remembers his transgressions no more.
t061.s3.h: The Son Is Mercy, the Spirit Ministers
t061.s3.i2: The Infinite Spirit inclines toward the Son's attribute of mercy and becomes the mercy minister of the Paradise Deities throughout the grand universe.
t061.s3.i4: Justice is the collective attitude of the Trinity, and mercy is the personal expression of that righteousness.
t061.s3.i5: Creator Sons are inherently merciful, yet through their bestowal experiences they acquire understanding mercy in a new way.
t061.s3.i6: Our superuniverse of Orvonton is a demonstration of love and mercy, noted for justice tempered by mercy and power conditioned by patience.
t061.s4.h: The Record and Limits of Mercy
t061.s4.i1: The Memory of Mercy is a living record of the mercy ministry extended to an individual, read as testimony at the adjudication of survival.
t061.s4.i3: Yet for one sincere of purpose and honest of heart, the credit of mercy is always far greater than he could ever exhaust.
t061.s4.i4: When endless mercy and patience are exhausted, justice prevails, and what mercy cannot rehabilitate justice will eventually annihilate.
t061.s5.i1: Mercy is a quality of growth: one can be truly merciful only after first becoming just, fair, patient, and kind.
t061.s5.i4: The mercy Jesus spoke of is not passive pity but active and dynamic, the supreme fatherly loving-kindness.
t061.s5.i5: Disciples are saviors, not judges of men, so they must first show their brothers the mercy they themselves would desire.
t061.s5.i6: The rule of the kingdom is that mercy determines judgment and love determines conduct, not the reckoning of giving and receiving.
t062.sum: Justice is the application of law; it is not the personal attitude of any one Deity but a collective function of the Paradise Trinity. The Ancients of Days and the Trinity-origin Sons render its verdicts, the personalities of the Infinite Spirit supply the evidence, and justice is always tempered by mercy. Man's idea of justice evolved from blood vengeance to the courts of the state, and Jesus taught that justice should be left to the group while the individual shows mercy.
t062.s1.h: A Collective Function of the Trinity
t062.s1.i1: Law issues from the Father, its administration belongs to the Son, its revelation and interpretation to the Spirit, and justice, the application of law, to the Trinity.
t062.s1.i3: Evidence for fairness is presented by personalities of the Infinite Spirit, and verdicts are rendered by the stationary Sons of the Trinity.
t062.s1.i4: The Ancients of Days render the decisions of supreme equity in the seven superuniverses, but in perfect Havona this function exists only in theory.
t062.s1.i5: The Supreme Trinity Personalities represent justice throughout the grand universe and function as the executive judgment of the Trinity.
t062.s2.h: The Justice and Fairness of God
t062.s2.i2: It is futile to plead with God to escape the just results of natural law and spiritual mandates, for one reaps what one sows.
t062.s2.i3: Mercy guides God's attitude toward the individual, while fairness guides his attitude toward the whole.
t062.s2.i5: When fully understood, the righteous justice of the Trinity and the merciful love of the Father coincide as one.
t062.s3.h: The Execution of Justice and Its Delay
t062.s3.i1: The final result for a being wholly identified with sin is annihilation, but its execution is delayed until the appointed processes of justice are fulfilled.
t062.s3.i2: Between identification with sin and the execution of the sentence there must be time enough to satisfy all concerned, even the sinner himself.
t062.s3.i4: The seraphic advocate of the courts is the mortal's defender, representing the element of mercy inherent in justice, the fairness that knows motives and tendencies.
t062.s3.i5: At the adjudication of survival the Memory of Mercy is read, and justice prevails only when mercy has been exhausted.
t062.s4.h: Justice as It Evolved in Human Society
t062.s4.i2: Man's idea of justice is getting his rights; though latent in the spirit-endowed mind, it grew by evolution.
t062.s4.i3: Primitive society substituted trial by ordeal and blood vengeance for justice, ignoring motive and judging only by the injury inflicted.
t062.s4.i4: The true administration of justice begins when vengeance is taken from the individual and the kin and given to the state.
t062.s4.i5: It gradually became clear that the certainty and swiftness of punishment deter crime more than its severity.
t062.s5.i2: A magistrate's duty is not only to punish the guilty but to acquit the innocent, so that injustice befalls not even the humblest citizen.
t062.s5.i3: The individual should show mercy, but fixing punishment should be left to groups and their representatives who know all the circumstances.
t062.s5.i4: Jesus possessed a firm sense of justice, but it was always tempered by mercy, and he recognized society's right to punish criminals.
t063.sum: Service is one way in which divinity is revealed on the personal level: the Son serves mankind, and the Infinite Spirit and his children possess by nature the urge to minister. For man, service is the social fruit of true religion, the inner experience of loving God flowing out as loving service to one's fellows. Jesus showed by washing feet that the one who serves is great, and the path of ascension leads on into endless universe service.
t063.s1.i1: On personality levels creatures can comprehend divinity as love, mercy, and ministry.
t063.s1.i3: Ministry to mind is the essence of the Infinite Spirit, and all his spirit offspring share the divine urge to serve.
t063.s1.i4: The family of the Infinite Spirit is forever devoted to ministering the love of God and the mercy of the Son, becoming a living ladder by which mortals ascend.
t063.s1.i5: The attributes of mercy and service displayed by the descending Sons derive from the Eternal Son.
t063.s2.i2: One who has found God seeks out and serves less enlightened fellows, not to boast but out of overflowing goodness.
t063.s2.i4: Jesus taught religion as the cause and ethics and service as the effect; inner religion shows itself in practical social service.
t063.s2.i5: Religion becoming a personal experience is not dangerous so long as it does not lose the motive of unselfish social service.
t063.s2.i6: Contact with the Adjuster is fostered by meditation, but it occurs more often in loving service to one's fellows.
t063.s3.h: The Way of Service Jesus Showed
t063.s3.i1: At the Last Supper, before apostles quarreling over places, Jesus knelt like a servant and washed the feet of all twelve, even Judas.
t063.s3.i3: The lesson of the foot washing was that the secret of greatness in the spiritual kingdom differs from the methods of power in the material world.
t063.s3.i5: Jesus asked not for sacrifice but for loyalty; service rendered by a friend for a friend cannot be called sacrifice.
t063.s3.i6: Even a small loving service, like a cup of cold water given to a thirsty soul, is always recorded by the Father's messengers.
t063.s4.i2: The profit motive should not be abolished suddenly but gradually transformed into unselfish motives.
t063.s4.i3: Apart from parental instinct, altruism does not arise spontaneously, so an unselfish social order requires the impulses of reason, morality, and religion.
t063.s4.i4: True parents engage in continuous service-ministry that their children, as they grow, will come to recognize and appreciate.
t063.s4.i5: The social service and intellectual fellowship of believers are precious, but as by-products of inner transformation they cannot replace the proclamation of the gospel.
t063.s5.i1: On the fourth mansion world ascenders first experience a social order based on the love of mutual service rather than selfish conquest.
t063.s5.i2: What the Father and the Sons bestow on us we bestow in turn on our fellows and the Supreme; the experience of love, joy, and service is mutual.
t063.s5.i3: Entry into the Mortal Corps of the Finality is the beginning of eternal service to the Paradise Trinity.
t063.s5.i4: In the present universe age the finaliters return to the universes of time and serve in one superuniverse after another.
t064.sum: Wisdom goes beyond knowledge to embrace facts and ideals, the relationships and meanings of things. God's wisdom exists perfectly in his infinite insight, but human wisdom evolves through experience, through trial and error, and especially through adjustment to failure. The adjutant spirit of wisdom lays its foundation, the Adjuster and the Spirit of Truth lead it toward truth, and in time thinking leads to wisdom and wisdom to worship.
t064.s1.i2: Because of the discrimination of infinite wisdom, God can be both just and merciful at the same time in any situation.
t064.s1.i3: Wisdom has a dual origin: the divine insight of perfect beings and the personal experience of evolutionary creatures.
t064.s1.i4: Superuniverse administration always associates the Perfectors of Wisdom, with their divine insight, and ascendant personalities seasoned by experience.
t064.s1.i5: Infinite wisdom ordains that anything be done in the best way, the right way, in the circumstances.
t064.s2.h: The Foundation of Wisdom in Mind
t064.s2.i1: The spirit of wisdom is the highest of the adjutant mind-spirits, coordinating the work of all the others.
t064.s2.i3: Animals may possess knowledge, but only man has the potential of wisdom that weaves ideas from memory.
t064.s2.i4: Wisdom is consciousness in which knowledge is elevated to new levels of meaning and activated by the adjutant of wisdom.
t064.s3.h: Wisdom Distinct from Knowledge and Truth
t064.s3.i2: Science leads to fact-consciousness, religion to value-consciousness, and philosophy, or wisdom, to the co-ordinating consciousness that embraces both.
t064.s3.i3: Science classifies men and religion loves men, but wisdom does justice to differing men.
t064.s3.i4: When the viewpoints of material fact and spiritual value are harmonized, wisdom interprets universe phenomena through progressive personality experience.
t064.s3.i5: Knowledge is gained by education, but the wisdom true culture requires comes only through experience; intelligence controls civilization, and wisdom directs it.
t064.s4.i2: Neither the idealist who ignores facts nor the materialist without spiritual outlook is wise, but only the one who adjusts facts to ideals.
t064.s4.i3: Knowledge, culture, and wisdom are different, and wisdom always dominates knowledge and glorifies culture.
t064.s4.i4: Wisdom is superknowledge; when people pool their minds, they can share each other's insight and avoid prejudice and narrowness.
t064.s4.i5: Jesus told James that true wisdom embraces discretion as well as courage.
t064.s5.h: From Wisdom to Faith and Worship
t064.s5.i1: Reason, wisdom, and faith are man's three highest attainments, and in the higher philosophy wisdom becomes allied to faith.
t064.s5.i2: True wisdom counsels allowing faith to accomplish what knowledge and reason cannot.
t064.s5.i3: The superphilosophic wisdom of the enlightened recognizes that to doubt God is to be untrue to the indwelling Adjuster.
t065.sum: Morality is the capacity unique to human personality to discern right from wrong and to judge the worth not only of means but of ends, and it distinguishes man from the animal. It evolved from self-conscious reason and grows not by law or force but by personal choice and influence. Morality is a prerequisite of religion but not the whole of religious experience, and the highest moral choice is the choice to do the will of God.
t065.s1.i2: Man can exercise moral insight before exploration or experiment, and only personality knows what it is doing before it does it.
t065.s1.i3: Intellect only selects means, but a moral being discerns the value of the ends themselves.
t065.s1.i4: One who cannot discern the goal of his strivings lives on the animal level and has failed to use the advantages of personality.
t065.s1.i5: A child's first moral choice appears with the seventh adjutant mind-spirit, and only after it is registered is an Adjuster assigned.
t065.s2.i2: Choosing between good and evil is influenced not only by moral keenness but also by ignorance, immaturity, and delusion, so a sense of proportion and the art of measurement are needed.
t065.s2.i3: Moral conduct is the highest performance of intellect: choosing higher ends and choosing moral means suited to those ends.
t065.s3.i1: Morality arose from self-conscious reason; it transcends the animal but is wholly evolutionary.
t065.s3.i2: Through the long and wasteful struggle to placate ghosts, man became conscious of relative right and wrong, and thus ethics was born.
t065.s3.i3: Early feelings of duty grew out of emotional fear, but the urge to unselfish service comes from the indwelling divine spirit.
t065.s3.i5: Static ethics and traditional morality are only slightly above the animal level; ethics becomes truly human when it is dynamic and progressive.
t065.s4.i2: The morality of evolutionary religion drives men by fear, but revealed religion draws them by a loving desire to be like God.
t065.s4.i3: As religion evolves, ethics becomes the philosophy of morals, and morality becomes the discipline of self by the standards of supreme spiritual ideals.
t065.s4.i4: A religion that stresses an isolated morality apart from truth and beauty fails to win the loyalty of modern people.
t065.s4.i5: Jesus did not put ethics in the place of religion; he taught religion as the cause and ethics as the result.
t065.s5.i2: Morality is a matter of the personality's free will and must spread by the contagion of contact with morally fragrant persons.
t065.s5.i3: Jesus interpreted the golden rule on the levels of the flesh, feelings, mind, brotherly love, morality, and spirit, teaching at the highest to treat people as God would treat them.
t065.s5.i4: Primitive man's neighbor was only those near him, but Jesus extended the neighbor to all mankind and even to enemies, and the human heart knows this is right.
t065.s5.i5: In the ages of philosophy and brotherhood people become truly moral beings and learn to live by the golden rule.
t066.sum: Sin is not mere imperfection or mistake but the attitude of a personality that knowingly and deliberately resists the Father's will and divine reality: deliberate disloyalty to God. The moral responsibility for sin is wholly personal and is not inherited, and no one loses survival because of another's sin. All sin can be forgiven, but a personality that has become wholly identified with sin becomes unreal and eventually reaches extinction.
t066.s1.i2: Error is the misunderstanding of reality, evil a partial maladjustment to reality, and sin a purposeful resistance to divine reality.
t066.s1.i3: Error reveals a lack of intellectual keenness, evil a deficiency of wisdom, sin spiritual poverty, and iniquity failing personality control.
t066.s1.i4: Good is the carrying out of the divine plan; sin is a deliberate rebellion against the divine will.
t066.s2.i1: The natural evil tendencies and imperfections of a person before rebirth are neither sin nor iniquity but only the starting point of the ascending journey.
t066.s2.i2: Finiteness in itself is neither evil nor sinful; evil and sin arise when the finite is misused and distorted.
t066.s2.i3: A sense of guilt is only the awareness of having violated a moral code and does not necessarily mean sin; there is true sin only in conscious disloyalty to God.
t066.s2.i4: The capacity to feel guilt is not a badge of human degradation but a mark of a being with potential greatness.
t066.s2.i5: Sin reveals the immaturity of one dazzled by the liberty of the will who fails to realize the obligations of universe citizenship.
t066.s3.h: Consequences of and Responsibility for Sin
t066.s3.i1: The effects of sin are never local, but sin is fatal to survival only when it becomes the whole attitude of mind and soul.
t066.s3.i3: No being's sin can prevent another's survival; eternal survival is jeopardized only by one's own choosing.
t066.s3.i5: Repeated sin becomes habit, and the habitual sinner can easily slip into iniquity and become a wholehearted rebel against the universe.
t066.s4.i1: God loves the sinner as an eternal personality reality, but sin is neither a person nor a spiritual reality, so only justice takes cognizance of it.
t066.s4.i3: A being wholly identified with sin becomes unreal and self-destroying, and once the sentence of extinction is executed, it becomes as if it had never been.
t066.s5.h: The Evolution and Correction of the Idea of Sin
t066.s5.i1: For primitive man sin was the violation of a ghost-sanctioned taboo, and death was regarded as its penalty.
t066.s5.i2: Primitive sin was an act, not a thought, and ceremonial; it gave rise to the belief in a fall from a perfect beginning.
t066.s5.i3: Sacrifice for personal sin gradually developed into the doctrine of atoning sacrifice for the sins of the race.
t066.s5.i4: Jesus did not die to atone for the racial guilt of mankind or to appease the wrath of God.
t066.s5.i5: Confession of sin does not remove its temporal consequences, but it is essential to religious growth and spiritual progress.
t067.sum: Evil is not created by God; it is the shadow cast when immature creatures in an imperfect finite world reject the light or choose wrongly. Evil is the unintended transgression of the Father's will and so differs from sin; when deliberately embraced, it becomes sin. Potential evil is necessary for free will and moral choice, but actual evil need not be experienced, and God brings ultimate good even out of the evil of time.
t067.s1.i1: God is so positively good that there is no room for negative evil in him, and he does not create evil.
t067.s1.i4: Evil is a partial realization of, or maladjustment to, universe reality and indicates a deficiency of wisdom.
t067.s1.i5: Evil is the misapplication of plans and the maladjustment of techniques, producing universe disharmony and planetary confusion.
t067.s2.i2: Evil arises from observing the imperfections in the shadow cast when a finite universe obscures the living light of the Infinite.
t067.s2.i3: Error is the inevitable shadow of incompleteness cast upon the ascending path toward Paradise perfection, not an actual universe quality.
t067.s2.i4: For relative good to appear, contrast with comparative evil, an imperfection that is not sin, is always necessary.
t067.s2.i5: Ascending the universe scale, goodness increases and evil decreases, but the possibility of experiencing evil remains until final spirit levels are attained.
t067.s3.i1: For evolving man to be free he must be able to err; the only world without the possibility of error is one without free intelligence.
t067.s3.i2: By giving the power to choose between truth and error, the Father created potential negation, but evil actually exists only when creatures choose it.
t067.s3.i4: The finite mind's imperfect comprehension of the infinite is itself potential evil; when it is not corrected and error grows, it becomes actual evil.
t067.s3.i5: Evil deliberately chosen becomes sin, and the persistent pursuit of sin and error becomes iniquity.
t067.s4.i3: All inner conflict is evil because it inhibits the creative function; it is a kind of civil war within the personality.
t067.s4.i4: Suffering is latent in evil, but much suffering has come from sin and iniquity, and the Father does not send suffering as punishment.
t067.s4.i5: Man should not blame God for the results of his own choices but should overcome earthly suffering through intelligent effort.
t067.s5.i1: For creatures to be truly free, the possibility of evil and sin is unavoidable, and the rulers do not deprive any being of freedom.
t067.s5.i2: The Father allows good and evil to grow together, like wheat and tares, until the end of life.
t067.s5.i3: The Melchizedeks teach that the good resulting from the Satania rebellion is more than a thousandfold the sum of all the evil.
t067.s5.i4: As wisdom grows through ascension, one better understands how ultimate good arises out of time-limited evil.
t067.s5.i5: Even man's experience of evil is part of God's unending self-realization in the children of time.
t068.sum: God's forgiveness flows naturally from his infinite understanding; it is given before man asks and requires no intermediary or sacrifice. Yet this forgiveness becomes real in personal religious experience only when one forgives one's fellows. Jesus taught to forgive even seventy times seven, and he said that inability to forgive others is a mark of immaturity that has not attained understanding and love.
t068.s1.i2: At the bottom of God's goodness lies the universal tendency to love, show mercy, manifest patience, and minister forgiveness.
t068.s1.i3: The Father is not a personality divided between justice and mercy, and he requires no mediator in order to forgive.
t068.s1.i4: Divine forgiveness is an inevitable consequence inherent in God's infinite understanding, his full knowledge of his children's errors and choices.
t068.s1.i5: The understanding love of wise parents usually prevents the very estrangement that would call for repentance and forgiveness.
t068.s2.i1: Divine forgiveness is the renewal of severed relations of loyalty; it need not be sought, only recognized and accepted.
t068.s2.i3: God's forgiveness is in fact unconditioned, but in experience it becomes real only when one forgives one's fellows.
t068.s2.i4: In forgiving his brother, a person creates in his soul the capacity to receive God's forgiveness of his own misdeeds.
t068.s2.i5: Faith is the price of entrance into God's family, and forgiveness is the act of God in accepting that faith.
t068.s2.i6: Jesus taught that forgiveness of sin is received by faith in God, without penance or sacrifice.
t068.s3.i2: When Peter asked whether seven times was enough, Jesus answered to forgive even seventy times seven.
t068.s3.i3: With the parable of the steward forgiven a great debt by the king who would not forgive his fellow's small debt, he taught the duty of the forgiven.
t068.s3.i4: The better one understands a neighbor, the easier it is to forgive; when one loves a brother, one has already forgiven him.
t068.s4.i2: People hold grudges and nurse vengefulness in proportion to their ignorance of others' inner nature and longings.
t068.s4.i3: All sin can be forgiven, but it is doubtful that a confirmed iniquitous person would ever truly sorrow or accept forgiveness.
t068.s4.i4: Those who knowingly and maliciously attribute the works of God to the forces of evil can hardly obtain forgiveness.
t068.s4.i5: The Father is not an indulgent parent who overlooks everything; he does not condone his children's self-destructive conduct.
t068.s5.h: Forgiveness in History and the Example of Jesus
t068.s5.i1: In primitive religion confession and forgiveness were a meaningless ritual that forgave in advance even the sins of the following week.
t068.s5.i2: Hosea preached forgiveness through repentance, not sacrifice, and revived the gospel of love and divine mercy.
t068.s5.i3: Before Jesus, a God who forgives repentant sinners was known, but a God who goes out first to seek the lost sheep was new.
t068.s5.i5: Peter, who had denied the Master, fully believed he was forgiven only after the risen Jesus received him again.
t069.sum: Fear was a powerful emotion that bound primitive man into society and prepared the first soil of religion, but unreasoned fear and worry now become poisons that hinder the progress of the soul. Revealed religion and the Thought Adjuster seek to change the fear of God into love and trust, and Jesus taught that foresight and prudence are permitted but that worry and anxiety should be abandoned for trust in the Father. His peace is a peace that keeps the heart from being troubled or afraid.
t069.s1.i1: Early man lived in constant fear of bad luck, and that fear had a paralyzing power.
t069.s1.i2: If hunger and love drew men together, vanity and ghost fear held primitive society together.
t069.s1.i3: It was not the sanctity of life but the fear aroused by the shock of death that fostered primitive religion.
t069.s1.i4: The false fears of primitive religion prepared the soil of the mind, and the Adjusters have ever since been transforming fear into the love of God.
t069.s1.i5: Evolutionary religion drives men by fear, but revealed religion leads them to seek a God of love through the longing to be like him.
t069.s2.i2: Mental poisons such as fear, anger, envy, and suspicion, like physical poisons, greatly hinder the spiritual progress of the soul.
t069.s2.i3: The emotion in man that angels find hardest to understand is the inheritance of animal fear that throws even faith into panic.
t069.s3.i1: Jesus did not forbid prudent foresight for the future, but he opposed worry and anxiety.
t069.s3.i2: Anxiety cannot add a cubit to one's stature or a day to one's life, so trust the Father who feeds even the ravens.
t069.s3.i3: He counseled not to be overanxious about needs but to spread them before the Father with prayer and thanksgiving.
t069.s3.i4: To Martha, troubled about many things, he said that the small things of life must give way to the greater things of the kingdom.
t069.s3.i5: People spend much time crying in fear like lost children, though in fact they are not far from safety.
t069.s3.i6: Returning from rest in the hills, the apostles realized that many pressing problems were the products of exaggerated fear and anxiety.
t069.s4.i1: Jesus told a fear-ridden young man to make his mind not a slave of fear but a courageous ally in solving problems.
t069.s4.i2: When the indwelling spirit is freed from the fetters of fear, the consciousness of being a child of God overcomes the fear of men.
t069.s4.i4: The anxiety arising from the fear of being alone in the universe should be dissolved by the contemplation of faith in the Father and the rest of worship.
t069.s4.i5: Happy and effective people are motivated not by fear of wrongdoing but by love of right doing.
t069.s4.i6: Mere belief may not overcome doubt and fear, but living faith always triumphs over doubting.
t069.s5.i1: Jesus knew no fear; he faced the realities of life without fear and was always cheerful and glad.
t069.s5.i2: The peace of Jesus is not passive calm but a peace that keeps the heart from being troubled or afraid amid trials and persecutions.
t069.s5.i4: On the morontia worlds ascenders learn to accept challenges without complaint and to face difficulties and uncertainties without fear.
t069.s5.i5: Teachers are exhorted to proclaim the love of God that casts out all fear.
t070.sum: True happiness comes from the inner life rather than from wealth or environment, and it is achieved when the selfish desires and the unselfish urges of the indwelling spirit are reconciled in one will. The highest happiness is inseparable from spiritual progress, and joy is experienced not alone but in sharing love and service. Jesus was not a man of sorrows but a man of gladness, and his peace is the joy and satisfaction of one who does the will of God.
t070.s1.i2: Happiness is the sum of techniques for gratifying natural urges in better ways, and it does not depend greatly on environment.
t070.s1.i3: Human happiness is achieved when the desires of the self and the unselfish urges of the higher self, the divine spirit, are coordinated in one will.
t070.s1.i4: Health, mental efficiency, and happiness arise from the unification of body, mind, and spirit.
t070.s2.i1: The highest happiness is inseparable from spiritual progress, and spiritual growth yields lasting joy and a peace that passes understanding.
t070.s2.i2: The Adjuster respects the value of selfish motives but gives weight to the unselfish urges that lead to happiness and the joys of the kingdom of heaven.
t070.s2.i3: One born of the spirit is released from the bondage of self-denial and translated into the joyous kingdom of the spirit.
t070.s2.i5: There is an inherent joy in freewill existence independent of all external influences, and the angels of the joy of existence strive to demonstrate it.
t070.s3.i1: The sermon on the beatitudes opened on the keynote of happiness, and its faith and love strengthen character and create happiness.
t070.s3.i2: A child's happiness is immediate pleasure, but an adult sows seeds of self-denial for greater happiness.
t070.s3.i3: Those who humbly seek God do not wait for distant rewards but experience the happiness of the kingdom in their hearts now.
t070.s3.i4: Asked why some are happier than others, Jesus answered that much depends on willingness to be led by the Father's indwelling spirit.
t070.s3.i5: Much sorrow comes from thwarted ambition and wounded pride, so after doing one's best one should accept one's lot and exercise ingenuity.
t070.s4.h: The Joy of Love and Service
t070.s4.i1: The new commandment was meant not as a burden but as a new joy of sharing affection with one's fellows.
t070.s4.i3: Jesus showed a fear-ridden young man the paths of service and the highways of happiness that lead to the joy of loving activity.
t070.s4.i4: Loving service rendered with full affection becomes not a sacrifice but supreme joy.
t070.s4.i5: After Pentecost the believers broke bread together with gladness and singleness of heart, enjoying the spiritual joy of the brotherhood's fellowship.
t070.s5.i2: The peace of Jesus is neither stoic resignation nor vague optimism but the joy and satisfaction of one who has fully learned how to do the will of God.
t070.s5.i3: The religion of Jesus does not flee from this life but ennobles present living with the joy and peace of a spiritual state of being.
t070.s5.i4: Morontia life is about half work and half play, and it enjoys the humor of realizing how trivial many past worries were.
t070.s5.i5: Jesus regarded this world not as a vale of tears but as a vale of soul making, where eternal spirits are born.
